summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — STLAP.PA +15%, WTB.L +5%, SSE.L +4%, CNA.L +4%, ASM.AS +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (ADYEN.AS -13%, SY1.DE -10%, BTRW.L -6%, DSY.PA -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: STLAP.PA (+14.94%) — Stellantis Q3 results beat on revenue (€37.6B vs ~€36.9B est) with FY2026 guidance reaffirmed and positive 2027 industrial FCF target. Reports date the jump to Oct 28, so today's +14.9% may be partly follow-through. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: STLAP.PA is the Paris line of a large-cap European automaker, and no strategy lists it. The move was an earnings-gap catalyst, so any gap-size or RSI filter would likely have excluded it even if it had been in the universe.

top_movers.catalyst: Stellantis Q3 results beat on revenue (€37.6B vs ~€36.9B est) with FY2026 guidance reaffirmed and positive 2027 industrial FCF target. Reports date the jump to Oct 28, so today's +14.9% may be partly follow-through.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: STLAP.PA is the Paris line of a large-cap European automaker, and no strategy lists it. The move was an earnings-gap catalyst, so any gap-size or RSI filter would likely have excluded it even if it had been in the universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU/UK constituents (e.g. CAC40/FTSE100 names) to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-results gap ≥ +8% on ≥2× average volume within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up no WTB.L news dated 2026-10-29, so this is likely a technical, sector or UK-consumer rebound rather than a company-specific event.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Whitbread is a UK mid-cap (FTSE 250-type) hotel/restaurant operator, which the bot's strategies don't cover. A ~5% move without a catalyst is also unlikely to trip a news-reactive filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small UK/EU mid-cap leisure and hospitality watchlist to the momentum-trader universe, gated on a ≥1.5× 20-day average volume and a ≥+4% close, so the next analogue is scored instead of ignored.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 29 Oct. SSE's last update was the 1 Oct trading update, which kept guidance, and results are due 18 Nov. Likely a sector or UK utilities move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SSE is a FTSE 100 large-cap UK utility and no strategy includes it. With no discrete catalyst, a +4.3% sector-driven move also wouldn't trigger news-reactive or gap filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK/EU defensive-utilities basket (SSE.L, NG.L, CNA.L) to the momentum-trader universe, gated on sector breadth (e.g. ≥3 of 5 utilities up ≥2% on the day) rather than single-name news.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up no same-day article for CNA.L (Centrica, if the ticker is right), so this is likely a sector or energy-price move, which I couldn't confirm.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CNA.L is a UK large-cap utility/energy name that no strategy lists. With no identifiable catalyst, a +3.84% move would also be too small for a news-reactive or gap-up filter to fire.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'unowned top-decile mover' check that logs any FTSE 100/250 name with |move| ≥3.5% and volume ≥1.5× its 20-day average, and flags it for universe review after 3 recurrences in 30 days.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely follow-through after record Q3 results (€1,159M revenue, +45% y/y, AI demand, new €300M buyback, 2027 outlook above €5.7B). The results came out around Oct 27, so today's move is probably semi-equipment sector momentum. I found no same-day news.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASM International is a Dutch large-cap semiconductor-equipment name, and no strategy covers Euronext Amsterdam. The catalyst was also 1-2 days old, so any earnings-gate or gap filter had already expired.
top_movers.suggestion: Add Euronext Amsterdam semi-equipment names (ASM.AS, BESI.AS, ASML.AS) to the momentum universe. Also add a post-earnings-drift rule that allows entries up to 3 days after a results gap of at least +5% on volume of at least 1.5x average.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found. The move is likely a Q3 2026 results reaction or a sector-wide European bank rally. Q3 results were probably due around this date, but I couldn't verify them.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DBK.DE is a large-cap DAX financial that no strategy's universe includes. If the move was earnings-driven, a gap-up at the open would also have been blocked by earnings and gap filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap DAX/Euro Stoxx 50 banks to the momentum universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-results gap of +3% or more once the opening volume is at least 1.5x average.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a reaction to Adyen's Q3 2026 business update (around 28–29 Oct): probably a net revenue or volume growth miss against expectations. I couldn't confirm the exact figures or date.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Adyen is a large-cap Euronext Amsterdam fintech that no uk-eu strategy covers. It was also an overnight earnings gap, so the loss was booked at the open before any post-results signal could fire. A long-only bot couldn't short it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap AEX/Euro Stoxx 50 names to the uk-eu universe, and let the earnings-gate release names that gap ≤ -8% on ≥2× average volume into a short-side or avoid-list signal, so the bot can skip catching the falling knife.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found. The drop falls in Symrise's usual late-October Q3 reporting window, so a Q3 sales or guidance disappointment is likely. The search turned up no Q3 2026 coverage.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SY1.DE is a German mid/large-cap flavours and fragrances (consumer staples/chemicals) name that no strategy lists. If this was an earnings gap-down, it was also a catalyst move that opened at the low, leaving no entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a liquid DAX/MDAX staples and chemicals watchlist to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings-gate flag gap-downs of -5% or more on 2x average volume as no-trade or review signals.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-29. Searches turned up no company-specific announcement, so this is likely a UK housebuilder sector move on rates, gilts or housing-demand worries.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BTRW.L is a UK mid/large-cap housebuilder that no strategy includes, so no filter ever evaluated it. A -5.75% sector-driven drop with no gap-and-news signal would also be unlikely to trigger a momentum or news-reactive entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK housebuilder basket (BTRW.L, PSN.L, TW.L, BKG.L) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a sector-wide drop (e.g. ≥3 names down >4% the same day), so rate-driven selloffs are evaluated.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely a reaction to Q3 2026 results, due around 28-29 Oct. I couldn't confirm the release or its numbers. Prior Dassault reports on weak guidance and slow automotive/pharma demand also hit the stock.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DSY.PA is a Paris-listed European large-cap software name that no strategy covers. If it was results-driven, the gap came at the open, so post-open signals would have been too late.
top_movers.suggestion: Add European large-caps such as DSY.PA to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-results gap of -4% or worse within 30 minutes of the open. That only helps if the bot can short.
